headline: Highest risk is medium: marker can process documents while awesome-selfhosted is a non-executing knowledge list, so direct harm is limited but shared-content trust and compliance gaps remain.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default communication channel is documented between awesome-selfhosted and marker. awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while marker has no shared filesystem, MCP, or clipboard bridge shown. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies awesome-selfhosted content into marker as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared clipboard or message queue is introduced between them, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard flows.
Do not pipe list content into marker as system or developer text.
Use a provenance tag on any copied content.
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer that strips instruction-like markup before handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows sensitive data classes, filesystem sharing, or network egress. awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and marker has no read_filesystem or network_egress capability. With no shared workspace or outbound channel documented, leakage is not plausible from the pair alone.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared workspace containing secrets, leakage risk changes.
IF marker is wrapped by an external service that uploads document contents, the profile no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared folder.
Run marker on non-sensitive documents only.
Verify no wrapper adds upload or sync behavior.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface to conflict over. awesome-selfhosted is a static knowledge-management listing with no write permissions shown, and marker explicitly lacks write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shell execution. The pair cannot contend for mutable state in the documented configuration.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk appears.
IF marker is wrapped with additional write permissions, the current assessment no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep marker read-only.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Do not grant git write access to either agent.
requires-engineering: add lock-based coordination if writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a curated list, not an action-taking agent, so marker is unlikely to treat its output as authoritative instructions by default. The main pathway is manual or orchestrated copy of list content into document processing, which is unusual and low-blast-radius because neither agent can execute downstream actions.
conditions: IF an operator feeds awesome-selfhosted entries into marker as factual source text without review, errors can propagate.
IF marker output is later used as authoritative metadata in another system, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing extracted facts.
Label copied list entries as unverified source material.
Keep marker outputs out of automated pipelines.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification checks before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. awesome-selfhosted is a public open-source list and marker shows no data classes touched or network egress. With only these profiles, there is no identifiable compliance breach pathway.
conditions: IF either agent is used on regulated data, a separate compliance review is required.
IF a deployment adds logging or retention of document contents, compliance risk may emerge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair.
Document any retention settings before deployment.
Check whether a wrapper adds logging.
requires-engineering: map data flows against residency and retention requirements.
